title: Βόες καὶ ἄξων
part: The Oxen and the Axle (Chambry 70 · Perry 45)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 70 (= Perry 45). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Τοῦ δὲ ἄξονος τρίζοντος, ἐπιστραφέντες ἔφασαν οὕτως πρὸς αὐτόν· « Ὦ οὗτος, ἡμῶν τὸ ὅλον βάρος φερόντων, σὺ κέκραγας ; »
sentences.tr: Tou de axonos trizontos, epistraphentes ephasan houtōs pros auton· « Ō houtos, hēmōn to holon baros pherontōn, sy kekragas ; »
sentences.l: And the axle creaking, having turned round they spoke to it thus: « You there, we bearing the whole weight, are you the one screaming? »
sentences.i: But when the axle creaked, they turned round and said to it: « You there — we carry the whole load, and you are the one crying out? »
sentences.n: Two genitive absolutes frame the joke: the axle's creaking sets the scene, ἡμῶν … φερόντων ('while we carry') supplies the grievance. κέκραγας is a perfect with present force, from κράζω — 'you are screaming', with no past sense at all.

sentences.t: Οὕτω καὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἔνιοι, μοχθούντων ἑτέρων, αὐτοὶ προσποιοῦνται κάμνειν.
sentences.tr: Houtō kai tōn anthrōpōn enioi, mochthountōn heterōn, autoi prospoiountai kamnein.
sentences.l: So too some men, while others are toiling, themselves make a show of being worn out.
sentences.n: One more genitive absolute, μοχθούντων ἑτέρων. προσποιοῦνται with the infinitive is 'to pretend to'; κάμνω is to labour to the point of exhaustion, hence the pretence of exhaustion.
